paragraphs: Rabbi Yitzchak bar Abba bar Machsya.

He was a disciple of Rav. In [Yerushalmi Megillah, chapter 2, at the end of halakhah 2](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Megillah.2.2.6), he sat with Rav Chananel before Rav: one said יהודים and the other יהודיים. In [Berakhot, chapter 6, halakhah 6](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Berakhot.6.6), Yitzchak bar Abba bar Machsya and Rav Chananel are mentioned: one said, “Blessed is He she-natan,” meaning “who gave.” They went up to Rav’s house and heard bar Chona (read: Rav Huna), in Rav’s name, say “asher natan,” also meaning “who gave,” etc.[^1]

notes.text: The readings יהודים and יהודיים differ by one yod. Both שנתן and אשר נתן mean “who gave.” Hyman proposes Rav Huna in place of bar Chona.
